title: Randomized space is contained in nondeterministic space
statement: For every function $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RSPACE}(s) \subseteq \mathrm{NSPACE}(s)$. The randomized class requires a finite machine using space bounded by a constant multiple of $s$, with acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members and no accepting branches on nonmembers; the nondeterministic class requires a finite machine with that space bound that halts on every branch and accepts exactly the members.
